pages.title: How to Find DMC3 Character Models — DMC Rengine
pages.description: Find DMC3 character models through provenance-aware NBZ, PAC/PNST and MOD inspection instead of guessed filenames.
pages.summary: Find Dante, Vergil, Lady and other DMC3 character-related model resources by preserving archive/member/slot provenance and verifying candidate payloads with the canonical MOD reader. This route targets character-model search intent while keeping model identification separate from unrestricted editing or rebuild claims.

sections.heading: Start from the resource graph, not a guessed filename
items: Enter through the DMC3 archive hierarchy, preserve NBZ member and PAC/PNST slot provenance, and classify the materialized leaf resource before calling it a character model.

When the payload is MOD, the canonical reader exposes hierarchy, transforms, meshes, texture-facing state and skinning-related data strongly enough for evidence-bounded structural and visual inspection.
Character names can guide discovery, but a plausible filename or neighboring slot is not promoted as universal identity without corpus evidence.

sections.heading: Viewer and authoring boundaries remain separate
items: DMC Native Reader can inspect promoted MOD resources on the current Android application surface, while DMC Rengine remains the canonical parser and evidence authority.
Finding and viewing a character model does not prove unrestricted geometry editing, universal conversion, animation rebinding or original-game acceptance of rebuilt files.
Keep model provenance attached so future extraction, comparison and reintegration workflows can trace the exact archive and container position from which the resource came.

pages.title: How to Find and Inspect DMC3 Enemy Models — DMC Rengine
pages.description: Find DMC3 enemy models through archive provenance and canonical MOD inspection without hard-coded universal paths.
pages.summary: Use the same evidence-aware archive-to-model pipeline for DMC3 enemy assets: locate the relevant NBZ member, preserve PAC/PNST slot provenance, classify the leaf payload and inspect MOD resources through the canonical reader. This gives enemy-model search intent a practical entry point without inventing one universal asset path.

sections.heading: Enemy discovery uses the same typed resource pipeline
items: Use GDSpaces to locate the archive member, preserve container and physical-slot identity, then classify the materialized payload before assigning model semantics.
For enemy resources that actually match MOD, the canonical reader exposes document, object and mesh structure, hierarchy, transforms, texture-slot relationships and skinning-related data.
Variants can reuse neighboring container layouts or related resources, so publishing one guessed slot or filename as universal identity would be weaker than preserving the observed provenance.

sections.heading: Inspection is stronger than guessing but weaker than authoring proof
items: Current read-side evidence supports structural and visual enemy-model inspection and can feed the Android Native Reader when the resource belongs to a promoted app module.
That does not authorize unrestricted model editing, universal animation binding or original-runtime acceptance of modified resources.
The technical MOD page remains the authority for format semantics; this guide exists to meet the practical user intent of finding and viewing enemy assets.

pages.title: DMC Native Reader for Android — Complete V142 Guide
pages.description: Complete NR-Luna-v73 Android guide through V142: formats, Stage Ops, effects, cutscenes, photo/video, gyro, ARCore, File Health and exact evidence limits.
pages.summary: Explore the Android NR-Luna-v73 development branch through V142: models and textures, assembled stages, motions, effects, collision, cutscenes and a virtual photo/video camera. This complete guide pins source 7f8caea and distinguishes implemented features from historical device tests and the older downloadable APK.

sections.heading: Choose an exact Android build
items: The Native Reader README identifies v68 / 1.0.41 as the promoted Android baseline. Its current source registry describes additional bounded modules beyond MOD, SCM, DDS and PTX; a source-module list is not an acceptance result for every downloadable APK.
The download catalog separately selects the public code-72 / 1.0.45 APK from source build 7d1188e. It is a debug/device-test artifact, not a stable release or a new physical-device acceptance result.
Use Downloads for the selected asset, source revision, size and SHA-256; use Capabilities and the pinned release notes for the operation and version you intend to use.

sections.heading: Start with a supported resource
items: MOD and SCM workflows cover model and scene inspection; DDS and PTX workflows cover texture and texture-bundle inspection. Check the selected build before relying on a specific viewing or navigation feature.

The practical MOD, SCM and texture walkthroughs currently identify Windows v1.0.0 Preview explicitly. Their UI instructions are not presented as an Android walkthrough or proof of Android/Windows parity.

Use the NBZ guide to prepare a materialized leaf resource while preserving archive/member/slot provenance. That separate extraction workflow does not imply NBZ unpacking, editing or repacking in Native Reader.
Unknown or unsupported inputs must remain unsupported rather than being assigned a guessed parser.

sections.heading: Other platform packages have their own limits
items: A public Windows x64 v1.0.0 technical preview provides release-documented read-only MOD, SCM, DDS and PTX viewing. It is an earlier snapshot than the newer Android line.
The public iOS IPA is an unsigned developer artifact requiring signing; its pinned evidence establishes build checks, not an app launched and accepted on iPhone.
Native Reader is read-only. Parsing, visual preview, editing, writing and original-game acceptance remain separate capabilities; compare them in the version-bound capability matrix.
